title: Quantitative Resolvent and Eigenfunction Stability for the Faber-Krahn Inequality: stability of the first Dirichlet eigenfunction (Theorem 5.2)
author: Mark Allen, Dennis Kriventsov, and Robin Neumayer
work: Quantitative Resolvent and Eigenfunction Stability for the Faber-Krahn Inequality
difficulty_reason: Supplying as context the paper's own main resolvent stability theorem (Theorem 1.2, source label thm: main, proved earlier in this same unit at source lines 929--976) and the qualitative concentration-compactness Proposition 5.1 (source label p:standard, source lines 993--1002), the counted proof still has to carry a source-local transfer from a resolvent estimate to an eigenfunction estimate that no qualifying examination asks for. It must pick the right-hand side f equal to the first ball eigenfunction scaled by its eigenvalue and read the main estimate as a combined bound on the exterior part of that eigenfunction and on the difference of the two solution operators; expand both u_Omega^f and the restriction of u_B in the Dirichlet basis of Omega and dominate the coefficient differences; convert that smallness into smallness of the weighted sum of the squared coefficients through the identity lambda_B b_k = lambda_{Omega,k} a_k coming from the equation satisfied by u_Omega^f; force a uniform spectral ratio for every k at least 2 by combining the ball's spectral gap with the qualitative Proposition 5.1; recover a lower bound for the first coefficient from the normalisation of u_B; and finally reassemble the squared L2 distance of the two first eigenfunctions from the pieces on Omega and on B minus Omega. Every step is carried by the paper's own theory of quantitative stability for the Faber-Krahn deficit rather than by quoting a textbook, which places this unit above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in the analysis of partial differential equations.
